transcript:
This message comes from Google Workspace with Gemini.
One subscription that does it all.
Personalized AI and premium business versions
of Gmail, Google Docs, Drive, and more.
Try it free for 14 days at goo.gle/workspacewithgemini.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump is back on the campaign trail today
in Perry, Georgia, rallying support for Republicans
ahead of the midterm elections.
Former President Barack Obama campaigns for Democrats
in Cleveland and Detroit.
With control of the Senate at stake,
four independent candidates are also competing for seats.
NPR's Barbara Sproun reports they share similar
political views but face very different races.
In Nebraska, Dan Osborne is making the case
that voters fed up with both parties
have a viable option in him.
The Democratic Party in the state thinks so too.
They supported him early on
and there's no Democrat on the ticket.
But the tables are turned in Montana
where independent Seth Bodner is in a three-way contest
with a Republican and Democrat.
State Democrats say that the race has split the party
with some rank and file supporting the nominee
and other prominent state Democrats supporting the independent.
Barbara Sproun, NPR News.
National Guard helicopters have been called in
to rescue people stranded on rooftops
amid historic flooding in New Mexico.
In Bloomfield, resident Amy Goodday says the San Juan River
flooded her family's home last night.
We were all freaked out and stuff
but one of us had to be the adult
and I was okay, we need to make a plan.
The family huddled on the roof of a trailer
until a police helicopter lifted everyone to safety.
Goodday says the most important thing
was getting her kids out alive.
I have my babies.
Everything else is replaceable but they are not.
More rain is expected across the region this weekend.
Forecasters say major flooding is expected
along the San Juan River at Shiprock
with a flood warning in effect through Sunday afternoon.
Stocks on Wall Street ended the week mixed
with the Dow Jones Industrial Average
posting a slight gain despite a sharp drop on Friday.
The NASDAQ and S&P 500 both lost ground for the week.
NPR's Rafael Naum reports concerns about rising oil prices
and artificial intelligence dominated trading.
The real action this week took place in the second half
when surging crude prices and intentions in the Middle East
sparked renewed fears about inflation
and the broader economy.
Rising energy costs have been a big drag on markets
ever since the war with Iran started earlier this year.
And then concerns about AI also resurfaced.
Meta said it would need to continue spending
massive amounts of money on AI
hammering stocks across the sector.
For investors, the main concern is whether
all this borrowing being done to pursue AI dominance
can be sustained, especially as interest rates are rising.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
This is NPR.
The Kingdom of Jordan has declared three days of mourning
after gunmen opened fire outside of a church Friday
killing seven people and injuring 40.
As NPR's Jana Raff reports, Muslims and Christians
are coming together to mourn the victims.
Outside a church in Amman, Muslims and Christians prayed
for the victims of Friday's shooting
in a predominantly Christian village near Carrick,
about 80 miles south of a capital.
Religious violence is extremely rare in Jordan,
which is predominantly Muslim.
Jordan imposed a reporting ban on the attack.
It said to quell incorrect information.
But the US Embassy issued a statement late Friday
saying Jordanian security forces
were continuing to search for the gunmen.
Police blocked off roads and posted security
outside other churches in the country,
as well as heightened checks in public places
such as shopping malls.
Jana Raff, NPR News, Amman.
Israel has closed roads into the occupied
West Bank city of Hebron today as troops searched the area
following attacks that killed two Israeli soldiers.
Palestinian officials say residents have been ordered
out of homes and the city's municipality reports
up to 300 families have left affected neighborhoods.
The Israeli military says the searches are focused
on the area where the gunmen operated.
Palestinians entering or leaving Hebron are being forced
to cross checkpoints on foot with vehicles barred
from the city's entrances.
This is NPR News.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone.
